notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).

name: TheAgentCompany: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Consequential Real World Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Simulates a software-company workplace to evaluate agents on professional tasks involving websites, programs, files, and coworker communication.

name: Mobile-Agent-E: Self-Evolving Mobile Assistant for Complex Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Uses hierarchical mobile agents and persistent tips and reusable action shortcuts to improve complex tasks from accumulated experience.

name: Plan-and-Act: Improving Planning of Agents for Long-Horizon Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Separates planning from execution and creates synthetic plan annotations for training agents on extended web-navigation tasks.

name: RealWebAssist: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Web Assistance with Real-World Users
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: RealWebAssist evaluates web assistance through sequences of instructions collected from real users across multiple websites. It tests intent interpretation, user-specific routines, long-term context, and visual grounding when instructions are ambiguous or evolve during interaction.

name: OSUniverse: Benchmark for Multimodal GUI-navigation AI Agents
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available.
summary: Introduces OSUniverse, a desktop GUI benchmark spanning precise clicks through multistep and multiapplication tasks. It provides both manual scoring and an automated validation mechanism.

name: MedBrowseComp: Benchmarking Medical Deep Research and Computer Use
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces MedBrowseComp, a benchmark of human-curated, multi-hop medical questions for agents retrieving and synthesizing facts from live knowledge bases in a computer-use setting.

name: ARPO:End-to-End Policy Optimization for GUI Agents with Experience Replay
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: ARPO extends group-relative policy optimization with a replay buffer that reuses successful GUI trajectories across training iterations. It filters tasks using baseline performance and compares end-to-end reinforcement learning with offline preference optimization on OSWorld.

name: SPA-RL: Reinforcing LLM Agents via Stepwise Progress Attribution
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Webshop is evaluated alongside ALFWorld and VirtualHome; the method is presented for general agents.
summary: Introduces SPA, a reward redistribution method for multi-step LLM agents that estimates each action’s contribution to task completion; Webshop is among its evaluations.

name: VideoCAD: A Dataset and Model for Learning Long-Horizon 3D CAD UI Interactions from Video
notes: The contribution was reviewed from the retained abstract. Sections 1 and 3 of the exact-version v2 paper identify Onshape as the browser-based interaction environment; the use of pixel-level input does not make the operated surface a desktop application.
summary: Introduces synthetic CAD interaction videos, a model for learning interface actions from video, and evaluation tasks for spatial and long-horizon reasoning.

name: WebChoreArena: Evaluating Web Browsing Agents on Realistic Tedious Web Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces WebChoreArena, 532 web chores built on WebArena environments to evaluate agents’ retention of page information, calculation, and tracking across pages.

name: Deep Research Bench: Evaluating AI Web Research Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces Deep Research Bench, 89 multi-step web research tasks and a frozen collection of scraped pages for evaluating search agents and their traces over time.

name: Thinking vs. Doing: Agents that Reason by Scaling Test-Time Interaction
notes: Reviewed against the complete official arXiv abstract.
summary: Test-Time Interaction scales the interaction horizon so web agents can explore, backtrack and revise plans within a rollout. Its online reinforcement-learning curriculum adjusts rollout lengths and is evaluated on WebVoyager and WebArena.

name: Atomic-to-Compositional Generalization for Mobile Agents with A New Benchmark and Scheduling System
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: UI-NEXUS evaluates compositional mobile tasks in local utility apps and online Chinese and English service apps. AGENT-NEXUS decomposes those long tasks into self-contained atomic subtasks to study generalization beyond isolated screens or short action chains.

name: Mirage-1: Augmenting and Updating GUI Agent with Hierarchical Multimodal Skills
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Mirage-1 organizes interaction trajectories into execution, core, and meta-skills, then uses them to guide Monte Carlo tree search during online GUI tasks. It introduces AndroidLH for long-horizon evaluation and tests the approach on Android and web-navigation benchmarks.

name: AgentSynth: Scalable Task Generation for Generalist Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: AgentSynth composes easily generated subtasks into longer computer-use tasks and trajectories with adjustable difficulty. Its evaluation uses the number of subtasks to probe how agent success changes as task complexity grows.

name: Mind2Web 2: Evaluating Agentic Search with Agent-as-a-Judge
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The benchmark assesses agentic search answers and source attribution.
summary: Introduces Mind2Web 2, 130 long-horizon tasks requiring live web browsing and information synthesis, plus an Agent-as-a-Judge framework for grading answers and sources.

name: MobileUse: A GUI Agent with Hierarchical Reflection for Autonomous Mobile Operation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: MobileUse reflects on errors at action and task timescales, invoking reflection when needed and using proactive exploration to learn unfamiliar apps. It evaluates this mobile execution framework on AndroidWorld and AndroidLab and describes a toolkit for physical-device operation.

name: NaturalGAIA: A Verifiable Benchmark and Hierarchical Framework for Long-Horizon GUI Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: NaturalGAIA builds verifiable long-horizon GUI tasks from human interaction intents while separating causal task structure from its verbal description. Its LightManus-Jarvis framework divides dynamic planning and context management from execution based on visual and structural interface information.

name: VeriWeb: Verifiable Long-Chain Web Benchmark for Agentic Information-Seeking
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The benchmark focuses on web information seeking and synthesis.
summary: Introduces VeriWeb, a benchmark of long-chain web information-seeking tasks with verifiable subtasks and a complete human-annotated trajectory for each task.

name: OdysseyBench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Complex Office Application Workflows
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces OdysseyBench for evaluating long-horizon workflows across office applications, plus HomerAgents to generate tasks from environment exploration and dialogue synthesis.

name: MMSearch-Plus: Benchmarking Provenance-Aware Search for Multimodal Browsing Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: Introduces MMSearch-Plus, a multimodal browsing benchmark with iterative image-text search, and an agent framework that marks and crops images for targeted retrieval.

name: FlashAdventure: A Benchmark for GUI Agents Solving Full Story Arcs in Diverse Adventure Games
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: FlashAdventure evaluates GUI agents on completing story arcs in 34 adventure games. It pairs an automated gameplay judge with COAST, a framework that keeps long-term clue memory to plan and complete sequential objectives.

name: AppCopilot: Toward General, Accurate, Long-Horizon, and Efficient Mobile Agent
notes: Trace reuse assumes stable layouts and fixed tasks. The described function-call routes are user-selected, and coordinate calibration depends on valid detected widgets. Basis: complete retained abstract and source-reviewed sections of the exact-version paper (4.2 OCR/OR Region Localization; 4.2.2 Coordinate Calibration; 4.3 Multi-Agent Voting; 5.2 Task Decomposition; 6.2 Experience Reuse; 6.3 Function Calling).
summary: Describes a mobile-agent stack combining region-based coordinate correction, hierarchical task planning, multi-agent voting, and reuse of successful interaction traces.

name: MobileRAG: Enhancing Mobile Agent with Retrieval-Augmented Generation
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: MobileRAG combines retrieval and memory components to support mobile tasks that need external knowledge or long action sequences. MobileRAG-Eval is introduced to study these requirements on complex real-world app tasks.

name: Instruction Agent: Enhancing Agent with Expert Demonstration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its reported success rate concerns a selected set of OSWorld tasks that other top-ranked agents failed.
summary: Introduces Instruction Agent, a GUI agent that follows instructions extracted from one expert demonstration and uses verification and backtracking to handle interruptions.

name: GUI-ReWalk: Massive Data Generation for GUI Agent via Stochastic Exploration and Intent-Aware Reasoning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUI-ReWalk begins with stochastic interface exploration and then infers goals to generate coherent action trajectories. It supports long-horizon workflows across applications and studies training on the resulting data using grounding and navigation benchmarks.

name: Recon-Act: A Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Browser-Use System via Web Reconnaissance, Tool Generation, and Task Execution
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract says the implementation has reached Level 3 of its proposed roadmap, with limited human intervention.
summary: Introduces Recon-Act, a browser-use framework that compares failed and successful web trajectories to create reusable tools for planning and executing long-horizon website tasks.

name: Scaling Agents for Computer Use
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces Behavior Judge, which converts execution trajectories into behavior narratives and compares multiple candidate rollouts. Experiments examine this selection approach on OSWorld, WindowsAgentArena and AndroidWorld.

name: Agent+P: Guiding UI Agents via Symbolic Planning
notes: Planning guarantees are relative to the modeled graph and selected target. They do not establish complete graphs, correct grounding or faithful goal translation. Basis: complete retained abstract and source-reviewed sections of the exact-version paper (3.3 UI Automation to Classical Planning; 4.1 UTG Builder; 4.2 Node Selector; 4.3 Plan Generator; 4.4 UI Explorer; 5.1 Datasets).
summary: Guides UI agents with symbolic planning over a UI transition graph initialized from app-code analysis and updated through online exploration, with evaluation on AndroidWorld.

name: ColorBench: Benchmarking Mobile Agents with Graph-Structured Framework for Complex Long-Horizon Tasks
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: ColorBench represents mobile tasks as graphs of states collected from real devices, providing a quasi-dynamic environment with multiple valid paths and error paths. It evaluates single-app and cross-app tasks using completion, subtask progress, and atomic diagnostics.

name: ColorAgent: Building A Robust, Personalized, and Interactive OS Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The abstract says current benchmarks are insufficient for comprehensive evaluation of OS agents.
summary: Presents ColorAgent, an operating system agent for long-horizon user instructions, trained with step-wise RL and self-evolving training and evaluated on AndroidWorld and AndroidLab.

name: Surfer 2: The Next Generation of Cross-Platform Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: Surfer2 combines hierarchical context management with separate planning and execution, self-verification, and recovery for visual computer use. It evaluates the framework across web, desktop, and Android tasks without task-specific fine-tuning.

name: MGA: Memory-Driven GUI Agent for Observation-Centric Interaction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces MGA, which separates task-agnostic screen-state reading from decision making and connects steps through structured state memory. Validated state deltas replace full trajectory replay, evaluated on OSWorld and application tasks.

name: Mobile-Agent-RAG: Driving Smart Multi-Agent Coordination with Contextual Knowledge Empowerment for Long-Horizon Mobile Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Uses separate retrieval systems for high-level mobile-task planning and precise interface operations, with a benchmark for extended cross-app tasks.

name: STEP: Success-Rate-Aware Trajectory-Efficient Policy Optimization
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: STEP allocates RL sampling by task success rate and trains on individual steps from interaction trajectories, with evaluations on OSWorld and AndroidWorld.

name: Training High-Level Schedulers with Execution-Feedback Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon GUI Automation
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: This work trains high-level schedulers with staged reinforcement learning driven by execution feedback. Its CES framework separates a Coordinator for planning and decomposition, a StateTracker for compressed context, and a low-level Executor.

name: AgentProg: Empowering Long-Horizon GUI Agents with Program-Guided Context Management
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces AgentProg, organizing mobile-agent interaction history as a program with variables and control flow to decide what context to retain. A global belief state handles partial observability, with evaluation on AndroidWorld and extended long-horizon tasks.

name: MobileWorld: Benchmarking Autonomous Mobile Agents in Agent-User Interactive and MCP-Augmented Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces long mobile workflows that combine agent-user interaction, cross-application tasks, and MCP-based tool access.

name: AndroidLens: Long-latency Evaluation with Nested Sub-targets for Android GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: AndroidLens provides 571 extended mobile tasks in Chinese and English, with multiple valid paths and preserved environmental anomalies. Its dynamic evaluation uses nested milestones and Average Task Progress to measure partial completion of long workflows.

name: ColorBrowserAgent: Complex Long-Horizon Browser Agent with Adaptive Knowledge Evolution
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ColorBrowserAgent converts human feedback into reusable website knowledge and uses that knowledge to guide progressive context summaries. It evaluates the resulting memory and adaptation mechanisms on long browser workflows.

name: Terminal-Bench: Benchmarking Agents on Hard, Realistic Tasks in Command Line Interfaces
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Terminal-Bench 2.0 benchmarks agents on 89 workflow-inspired tasks in computer terminal environments, with a distinct environment, human solution and verification tests for each task.

name: EvoCUA: Evolving Computer Use Agents via Learning from Scalable Synthetic Experience
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: EvoCUA combines task synthesis with executable validators, asynchronous sandbox rollouts and iterative policy updates. It turns successful routines and analyzed failures into supervision and evaluates the evolving agent on OSWorld.

name: OS-Marathon: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents on Vast-Horizon, Repetitive Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces OS-Marathon to evaluate long repetitive computer-use workflows whose execution grows with the amount of input data. It studies failure accumulation under task decomposition and GraphDemo, which adapts agents using a demonstration of the recurring workflow.

name: BEAP-Agent: Backtrackable Execution and Adaptive Planning for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: BEAP-Agent treats GUI execution as depth-first search with coordinated planning, execution and task-state tracking. It supports backtracking across multiple levels of earlier states and evaluates recovery on OSWorld.

name: Darwinian Memory: A Training-Free Self-Regulating Memory System for GUI Agent Evolution
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Darwinian Memory splits GUI trajectories into reusable units and updates the memory by retaining useful paths and pruning poor ones. It evaluates this training-free memory mechanism on long multi-application tasks.

name: LHAW: Controllable Underspecification for Long-Horizon Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: LHAW generates underspecified variants of long-horizon workflow tasks and uses agent trials to evaluate when missing information requires clarification.

name: ICA: Information-Aware Credit Assignment for Visually Grounded Long-Horizon Information-Seeking Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Information-Aware Credit Assignment scores intermediate information gathered by web agents, using rendered webpage snapshots to compare evidence across trajectories.

name: HiPER: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning with Explicit Credit Assignment for Large Language Model Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). WebShop is one of the interactive benchmarks reported for this general agent-training method.
summary: HiPER trains interactive LLM agents with separate subgoal planning and multi-step execution, assigning reinforcement-learning credit at both levels.

name: MemoryArena: Benchmarking Agent Memory in Interdependent Multi-Session Agentic Tasks
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MemoryArena links tasks across sessions so that agents must distill earlier interaction experience and use it in later decisions. Its evaluation includes web navigation alongside planning, search and formal reasoning, testing memory through subsequent actions rather than recall alone.

name: IntentCUA: Learning Intent-level Representations for Skill Abstraction and Multi-Agent Planning in Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: IntentCUA coordinates planner and critic agents through shared intent-aligned memory, retrieving reusable skills for long-horizon automation across desktop applications.

name: M$^2$: Dual-Memory Augmentation for Long-Horizon Web Agents via Trajectory Summarization and Insight Retrieval
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces M², a training-free memory framework for long-horizon web agents that summarizes interaction history and retrieves task guidance from an offline insight bank.

name: STRUCTUREDAGENT: Planning with AND/OR Trees for Long-Horizon Web Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: Introduces STRUCTUREDAGENT, a web-agent planning framework that interleaves execution with dynamic AND/OR trees, supporting node repair and exploration of alternative plans.

name: Hybrid Self-evolving Structured Memory for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces HyMEM, a graph-based memory for GUI agents that links symbolic task knowledge with trajectory embeddings and refreshes working memory during computer-use tasks.

name: AndroTMem: From Interaction Trajectories to Anchored Memory in Long-Horizon GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces AndroTMem-Bench for Android tasks whose later actions depend on earlier UI states. Anchored State Memory retains causally linked intermediate states for subgoal-specific retrieval and evaluates them against full-history and summary-based memory.

name: A Subgoal-driven Framework for Improving Long-Horizon LLM Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: The framework separates inference-time subgoal planning from MiRA, a reinforcement-learning method that supplies milestone rewards. WebArena-Lite experiments evaluate these mechanisms for long-horizon web navigation.

name: CarePilot: A Multi-Agent Framework for Long-Horizon Computer Task Automation in Healthcare
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: CareFlow benchmarks long healthcare-software workflows, while CarePilot coordinates action proposals, execution checks and corrective feedback using short- and long-term memory. Its actor consumes visual interfaces and system state to select semantic actions.

name: Vision2Web: A Hierarchical Benchmark for Visual Website Development with Agent Verification
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The benchmark evaluates website development by coding agents, with a GUI agent used for verification.
summary: Introduces Vision2Web, a benchmark for website development from images, spanning UI-to-code, multi-page frontend and full-stack tasks, with a GUI agent verifier and VLM-based judge.

name: When Users Change Their Mind: Evaluating Interruptible Agents in Long-Horizon Web Navigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Interruptions are evaluated through synthesized scenarios in a simulation framework.
summary: Introduces InterruptBench, a WebArena-Lite-derived benchmark that tests how long-horizon web-navigation agents handle mid-task user additions, revisions, and retractions.

name: AgentHazard: A Benchmark for Evaluating Harmful Behavior in Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces AgentHazard, a benchmark of harmful multi-step behavior by computer-use agents acting through tools, files, and execution environments.

name: GUIDE: Interpretable GUI Agent Evaluation via Hierarchical Diagnosis
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: GUIDE evaluates GUI trajectories by segmenting them into subtasks, diagnosing each segment, and aggregating structured findings into a task verdict. It tests diagnostic judgments on e-commerce, web-agent and Android-control traces rather than relying on one holistic trajectory score.

name: Gym-Anything: Turn any Software into an Agent Environment
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces Gym-Anything, where a setup agent configures software environments and an independent auditor checks the resulting evidence. CUA-World supplies long-horizon tasks across professional applications, with experiments on trajectory distillation and test-time auditing.

name: The Art of Building Verifiers for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Describes a web-trajectory verifier built around structured rubrics, separate process and outcome judgments, and explicit treatment of uncontrollable failures. CUAVerifierBench supplies human labels for evaluating these choices and screenshot-based context management.

name: GameWorld: Towards Standardized and Verifiable Evaluation of Multimodal Game Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its computer-use interface is evaluated through games, alongside a separate semantic-action interface.
summary: Introduces GameWorld, a browser-game benchmark that evaluates multimodal agents through keyboard and mouse controls or semantic actions using outcome checks.

name: CocoaBench: Evaluating Unified Digital Agents in the Wild
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces CocoaBench, a benchmark for unified digital agents on long-horizon tasks combining vision, search, and coding, including capabilities related to GUI automation.

name: UI-Copilot: Advancing Long-Horizon GUI Automation via Tool-Integrated Policy Optimization
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: UI-Copilot separates GUI execution from on-demand memory retrieval and numerical assistance. Its training procedure treats tool selection and multi-turn task execution as distinct optimization targets while keeping persistent observations outside transient context.

name: WebUncertainty: Dual-Level Uncertainty Driven Planning and Reasoning For Autonomous Web Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: WebUncertainty adapts planning mode to task uncertainty and guides action-level tree search with confidence-derived uncertainty estimates. Its evaluations examine autonomous execution of dynamic, long-horizon web tasks on WebArena and WebVoyager.

name: SOLAR-RL: Semi-Online Long-horizon Assignment Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its rollout candidates and step rewards are reconstructed from static data.
summary: SOLAR-RL trains GUI navigation agents by reconstructing rollout candidates from static data and assigning step rewards that reflect trajectory quality.

name: Odysseys: Benchmarking Web Agents on Realistic Long Horizon Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces Odysseys, a live-web benchmark of long, multi-site tasks derived from browsing sessions. Graded task rubrics and a rubric-score-per-step measure evaluate both partial progress and trajectory efficiency.

name: Step-level Optimization for Efficient Computer-use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Proposes a step-level model cascade that runs a smaller computer-use policy until learned monitors flag stalled progress or semantic drift. Separate history-based stuck detection and milestone checks determine when to escalate for recovery or verification without retraining the larger model.

name: Planner Matters! An Efficient and Unbalanced Multi-agent Collaboration Framework for Long-horizon Planning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Web navigation and OS control are among several benchmark settings for the general framework.
summary: A planner-centric RL framework divides agent automation among a planner, actor, and memory manager, with evaluations that include web navigation and OS control.

name: AcademiClaw: When Students Set Challenges for AI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: AcademiClaw benchmarks OpenClaw agents on long academic workflows, scoring task completion in isolated Docker sandboxes with rubrics and a safety audit.

name: cotomi Act: Learning to Automate Work by Watching You
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its reported task score uses the 179-task WebArena human-evaluation subset.
summary: cotomi Act is a browser agent that executes multi-step tasks and turns observed user browsing into persistent knowledge shared with users.

name: WebTrap: Stealthy Mid-Task Hijacking of Browser Agents During Navigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract reports experiments on browser-agent tasks based on extended WASP and InjecAgent environments.
summary: WebTrap injects mid-task instructions into browser-agent navigation to steer an agent toward an attacker goal before it resumes the user's task.

name: Mem-W: Latent Memory-Native GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces Mem-W, which compresses previous trajectories and current-session segments into latent memory tokens used directly by the GUI policy. Self-distillation and outcome supervision train this memory representation for web and mobile navigation.

name: WildClawBench: A Benchmark for Real-World, Long-Horizon Agent Evaluation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: WildClawBench evaluates CLI agents on long, multimodal tasks in Docker containers with real tools, using task checks, side-effect audits, and a semantic judge.

name: Executable Agentic Memory for GUI Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Executable Agentic Memory stores GUI routines in a knowledge graph built through state-aware exploration and action-group mining. A learned value model guides tree search over this executable memory for retrieval-based planning, with AndroidWorld and efficiency evaluation.

name: SaaS-Bench: Can Computer-Use Agents Leverage Real-World SaaS to Solve Professional Workflows?
notes: The complete retained official abstract and cached official README were reviewed.
summary: SaaS-Bench evaluates browser agents on professional workflows across self-hosted applications. Weighted checkpoints measure task completion and partial progress, with application-state checks and configured content judges documented in the official harness.

name: MementoGUI: Learning Agentic Multimodal Memory Control for Long-Horizon GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: MementoGUI learns a controller for selecting, compressing and retrieving textual and region-level visual memories while leaving the GUI-agent backbone fixed. It also converts computer-use traces into controller training data and evaluates semantic actions, progress and memory consistency on long-horizon tasks.

name: What and When to Distill: Selective Hindsight Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The method targets general multi-turn agents; WebShop is one of two evaluation environments.
summary: SERL trains multi-turn agents by using task rewards and selective step feedback to weight updates, with WebShop among its evaluation settings.

name: CutVerse: A Compositional GUI Agents Benchmark for Media Post-Production Editing
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Cutverse benchmarks GUI agents on long editing workflows across professional media applications and parses recordings and input logs into grounded action trajectories.

name: MemGym: a Long-Horizon Memory Environment for LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Computer use is one track among dialogue, research, and coding evaluations.
summary: MemGym benchmarks agent memory across several task regimes, including computer use on WebArena-Infinity, with scores designed to isolate memory performance.

name: Claw-Anything: Benchmarking Always-On Personal Assistants with Broader Access to User's Digital World
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Claw-Anything benchmarks persistent personal assistance across activity histories, backend services and integrated GUI/CLI interaction. Its simulated event histories introduce irrelevant or conflicting context, and a separate generation pipeline supplies training environments.

name: Anchor: Preventing Artifact Drift for Reliable Agent Verification
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The shared verifier scores end-state business correctness across several agent harnesses.
summary: Anchor builds ERP-Bench by generating procurement and manufacturing tasks with shared state verifiers for evaluating browser and computer-use agents.

name: AndroidDaily: A Verifiable Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agents on Real-World Closed-Source Applications
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: AndroidDaily evaluates mobile GUI agents on daily workflows in closed-source Android apps. Its GRADE evaluator follows visual trajectories against operational obligations, output-quality requirements and negative constraints, producing process-level diagnostics without hidden app state.

name: GTA: Generating Long-Horizon Tasks for Web Agents at Scale
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: GTA generates multi-hop web-agent tasks and executable trajectories through crawling, retrieval, and validation, releasing a benchmark built from over 50 websites.

name: Multi-Agent Computer Use

name: LongHorizonUI
notes: Code release of the ICLR 2026 paper "LongHorizonUI: A Unified Framework for Robust long-horizon Task Automation of GUI Agent" (the repository description says ICLR2026; the README cites it with anonymous authors and no link). Each screenshot passes through RapidOCR, the OmniParser v2 YOLO icon detector (downloaded from microsoft/OmniParser-v2.0 on first use) and template matching when an icon template directory is set; the merged elements are drawn as numbered boxes, and that annotated screenshot with a step prompt is what the Gemini, Azure OpenAI or OpenAI model receives. Actions are click, long press, swipe, drag, text input and key press. With the fallback cascade on (the default), an element-index target that fails is retried as a relative point inside the box and then as absolute coordinates with jitter; a progress monitor can roll back to the last committed snapshot, at most three times per task. The README documents only the offline mode, which replays a task's recorded screenshot sequence with either the task description or step-by-step instructions. run.py also has a live subcommand that lists USB-connected devices, but at the reviewed commit AndroidContext never opens a device connection (its context stays None), so device actions return without acting. The repository also has a Gradio app, agents that turn recorded taps and swipes into step descriptions, a scrcpy-based Android recording tool, step-level evaluation scripts and the project page source. The LongGUIBench dataset is not released (the README link is a placeholder), the requirements.txt the README installs from is not in the tree, and the README's Apache-2.0 badge and LICENSE link are not backed by a license file. Not a fork, not archived; no release. Code was read, not run.
